JUDGMENT

This present petition is filed under Sec.166 of MV Act 1989 injured minor petitioner through his natural guardian seeking compensation of .20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. It is case of the petitioner that: on 20-09-2023 at about 6.15 p.m. while his son was crossing the road near Mysore ground, Gokulam 3rd stage, Mysore, the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KL-59-D-1813 was riding the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and collided the petitioner.
As a result, the petitioner fell down and sustained severe injuries all over his body..
Immediately he was taken to Apollo Hospital, Mysore, where he has taken treatment as an inpatient and incurred .2,00,000/- towards medical and other incidental expenses.
The accident was caused due rash and negligent riding by the rider of the offending vehicle.

3. At the time of accident, Petitioner was aged 11 years and was a student .Due to the injuries sustained, he was unable to attend the school or participate in curricular and extra curricular activities, which has adversely affected his education and future prospects.

4. The Petitioner claims that the Respondents, being the owner and insurer of the alleged offending vehicle, jointly and severally liable to pay compensation along with interest for injuries, pain suffering and financial loss caused by the accident.
5. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the court through their counsel and filed their written statement.
The Respondent No.3 has not appeared before the court and he was placed exparte.

6. Respondent No.1-RC owner has filed his written statement denying the averments made in the petition inter alia contending that accident occurred due to negligence on the part of the petitioner and he was the responsible for the accident.
He stated that he is the owner of the offending vehicle and it was covered insurance with the Respondent No.2 and that policy was valid as on the date of accident.
The compensation claimed is exaggerated and prayed for dismissal of the petition.

7. The Respondent No.2-Insurance company has filed its written statement denying the averments made in the petition inter alia admitting the issuance of an insurance policy in respect of alleged offending vehicle , this respondent has disputed the validity as on the date of accident.
It has further contended that its liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.

This Rajkumar D vs Albin Joseph on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125463272/
2 respondent has also alleged that the owner of the offending vehicle has not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) of MV Act.

entities.text: Rajkumar D vs Albin Joseph on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has further contended that the rider of the offending vehicle did not possess the valid and effective driving licence on the date of accident.
It has denied the nature and extent of injuries allegedly sustained by the Petitioner, the treatment undertaken, the expenses incurred and disability suffered.
The compensation claimed is exorbitant.
For all these reasons, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

8. On the basis of the above, the following Issues arise for my consideration :-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that on 20-09-2023 at about 6-15 p.m., near Mysore one ground, Gokulam 3rd stage, Mysore, he sustained injuries in a road traffic accident, while he was crossing the road, due to the rash and negligent driving of rider of the motorcycle bearing number KL-59-D- 1813?
2. Whether the Respondent No.2 proves that, the policy conditions are violated by Respondent 1 and the Respondent No.2 is not liable to pay any compensation?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation if any, how much, from whom?
4. What order or award?
9.

In order to prove the claim, the natural guardian/father of Petitioner is examined as PW.1, the doctor who has assessed the disability of Petitioner is examined as PW-2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P-13.
On the other hand the Respondents have not chosen to adduce any oral and documentary evidence.

10. Heard arguments.
11.
Learned counsel for 2nd respondent has relied upon a citation reported in (2014) 14 SCC 396 - Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager, National Ins.Co.Ltd., and another and gazette notification..

entities.text: Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager, National Ins.Co.Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
12. By considering the evidences, arguments and the other materials available on record, I have answered the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: In the Negative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 13. ISSUE NO.1:- Since the Petitioner being minor, represented by his natural guardian/father and he is examined as PW-1.

PW-1 has stated in his chief- examination affidavit that the accident occurred due to negligent riding of the motorcycle by its rider and further he deposed that on Rajkumar D vs Albin Joseph on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125463272/
3 20-09-2023 at about 6.15 p.m. while his son was crossing the road near Mysore ground, Gokulam 3rd stage, Mysore, the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KL-59-D-1813 was riding the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and collided the petitioner.
As a result, the petitioner fell down and sustained severe injuries all over his body.
14. The father of Petitioner had given the first information statement to the Police as per Ex.P.2 on the basis of which Ex.P.1 FIR was registered.
Spot Mahazar and sketch was done by the Police as per Ex.P.3 and 4.
The offending vehicle was inspected as per IMV report at Ex.P6 and after completion of investigation, charge sheet is filed by the concerned Police as per Ex.P.7.

Ex.P.5 is the wound certificate, which shows that the Petitioner has sustained head injury, fracture left temporal bone,
fracture right tibia, left VII LMN paresis and injuries to other parts of the body.
15. The Respondent-Insurance company has contended that the accident occurred due to negligence of the petitioner.
During the course of cross examination of PW-1, it was suggested that his son was walking on the road hence the accident occurred.
he denied the same.
I have once again pursued the material available on record.

Except cross-examination and contention in the objections,
respondent no 2 - insurance company has not produced any evidence to disprove the negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.
There is no materials on record to disprove PW1 testimony and to prove the contention of the Respondent no 2.
The evidence of PW-1 corroborates with the documents produced.
It is well settled principle that Motor Vehicles Act is beneficial legislation, the tribunal need not to go for the strict proof of rash and negligence.
After the investigation, police have filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.
Ex.P.7 charge sheet prima-facie establishes the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The said charge sheet has not been challenged.
All the evidence and materials clearly indicates that it was negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.
Thereby the accident occurred and petitioner has sustained injuries in a RTA.

Hence I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
16. ISSUE No.2:-The respondent No.2
has taken contention that the owner of the offending vehicle has violated the terms and condition incorporated in the policy.

Therefore, the respondent No.2 is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner and respondent No.2-insurance company is absolved from its liability to reimburse the owner of the offending vehicle.
The onus of proof will be on the person who wants to rebut the presumption.
The Respondent no 2 has not chosen to lead positive evidence that its company is absolved from its liability to reimburse the owner of the offending vehicle.
Whatever, the contention raised by the Respondent no.2 in his written statement remains as pleading only.
They have not proved by the Respondent no 2.
It is settled principle of law that the allegation of the fact can be proved by providing evidence or by eliciting something from the mouth of the opponent.
Keeping in view of modes of proving an allegation of fact, again say that the Respondent no 2 has failed to prove his contention.

The offending vehicle was covered under a valid insurance policy, hence fastening joint liability on the Respondent no 2-insurance company Wherefore, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
Hence I answer this issue in the negative.

Rajkumar D vs Albin Joseph on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125463272/
4 17. ISSUE NO.3 :-The Petitioner was of 11 years old at the time of accident and sustained head injury, a fracture of left temporal bone, a fracture of right tibia, left VII LMN paresis and injuries to other parts of his body.
He was admitted to Apollo Hospital, Mysore, wherein he was treated as an inpatient and underwent surgery.

Due to the accidental injuries he was unable to attend the class,
cannot participate in co-curricular activities and it affects his future career.

18. PW-2 Dr.Banu Prakash A.S. Senior Consultant Neurosurgeon and spine surgeon at Shreyas clinic, Bengaluru has deposed that he examined the petitioner on 22-07-2024 for the purpose of assessing the disability.

He has stated that the petitioner has sustained the following injuries:
*Left ear bleed, *Inability to move right lower limb, *Confused E3-V5-M6, left ear bleed, *CSF otorrhoea, *Fracture left temporal bone pneumocephalus, *Posterior foss tentorium cerebelling SDH.
*Left facial nerve lower motor paresis, *Dislocation of the ossicle in left middle ear,
*Fracture of right tibia.
19. Further, PW-2 has stated that the Petitioner was treated with CRIF for a tibia fracture, and was diagnosed with left facial palsy, for which daily treatment was provided at home.

PW2 has also stated that the neurobehavioral disability was assessed 30% and the cognitive disability was assessed at 25% , using telescopic summation formula, the neuro - psychological disability was calculated at 46.66% and total body disability was assessed at 66%.

PW-2 has produced OPD record and neuro psychological assessment report at Ex.P.12 and 13.
20.
As it is held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court it is difficult to assess the compensation in the case of children sufferings from disability on account of motor vehicle accident.
21. With regard to disability, doctor has assessed the disability of whole body at 66%.
In his cross- examination, he denied that the petitioner is not facing any intellectual cognitive disability and neuro behavioral disability.

He admitted that as per EX P13 the IQ level of the petitioner is 76.
22.

Considering the tender age of the Petitioner and nature of injuries sustained by him, type of treatment obtained and testimony of doctor, the permanent functional disability to the whole body is assessed at 11%.
23. There is no materials on record to establish that the Petitioner has suffered any loss to his educational career as a result of the accident.
Accordingly no compensation is awarded under the head of loss of education due to the accidental injuries.
24. As held in the Master Mallikarjuna V/s Divisional Manager reported in (2014) 14 SC 396 if the disability is above 10% and up to 30% to the whole body, the compensation should be .3 lakhs.

entities.text: Master Mallikarjuna V/s Divisional Manager reported in (2014) 14 SC 396
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: For permanent disability up to 10%, it should be .1 lakh, unless there are exceptional circumstances to take a different yardstick.
In the present case whole body disability is assessed at 11%.

Considering Rajkumar D vs Albin Joseph on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125463272/
5 the age of the Petitioner and nature of injuries, I deem it proper to award .2,50,000/- for Pain and sufferings already undergone and to be suffered in future, mental and physical shock, hardship,
inconvenience and discomforts, etc and loss of amenities in life on account of permanent disability.

5

sentences.text: 25. Under the head of discomfort, inconvenience and loss of earnings to the parents during the period of hospitalization .1,00,000/- is awarded.
26. The PW1 has deposed that a sum of Rs.2,85,231 incurred towards medical and incidental expenses during the period of hospitalization.
In support of this, PW1 has produced the medical bills at Ex.P.9 amounting to Rs.2,85,231/-.
On perusal of medical bills, it reveals that parents of the petitioner incurred the amount of Rs.2,85,231/- towards medical expenses.

However, it has been brought on record that the IP bill at sl.no.1 and 32 amounting to Rs.1,64,682/- and Rs.66,371/-
respectively were paid by Star Health and allied Insurance Company Limited.

entities.text: Star Health and allied Insurance Company Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The other medical bills were not reimbursed and they appear to be genuine and hence, the petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.54,178/- towards medical expenses under just and reasonable compensation.

27. By considering the above judgment, and taking into consideration of all the materials produced by the Petitioner, this tribunal awards compensation under the following heads:
Sl.N HEAD COMPENSATION o.
1. Pain and suffering already . 2,50,000/- undergone and to be suffered in future, mental and physical shock, hardship, inconvenience and discomforts etc., and loss of amenities in life on account of permanent disability 2. Discomfort, inconvenience and . 1,00,000/- loss of earnings to the parents during the period of hospitalization 3.

Medical expenses . 54,178/-
TOTAL .4,04,178/-
28.
Liability: The policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Hence, the Respondent No.1 and 2 being the insured and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, in view of the issuance policy, the Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner with interest at 6% per annum.
With these observations, I have answered Issue No.3 Partly in the Affirmative.

reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with cost.

Petitioner is awarded compensation of .4,04,178/- together with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the realization.

Respondent No.2 shall pay the aforesaid amount within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of compensation amount, entire amount shall be kept in FD in the name of petitioner in any nationalized bank till he attains the age of majority or for a period of 2 years whichever is later.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
